questions.question: How does radio work, and when did radio broadcasting begin in South Africa?
questions.expected_answer: A radio station sends sounds, such as voices and music, through the air using invisible radio waves from a tall mast. A radio's aerial receives the waves and the radio turns them back into sound. Radio broadcasting began in South Africa in the 1920s, and the SABC was formed in 1936.

questions.question: Who showed one of the first television systems, and when did South Africa get television? Why so late?
questions.expected_answer: John Logie Baird, a Scottish inventor, showed one of the first working television systems in 1926. South Africa got television on 5 January 1976, much later than most countries, because the apartheid government worried that television would bring in ideas it did not want people to see.

questions.question: Give three ways radio and television changed people's lives.
questions.expected_answer: News travelled faster and people could see events as they happened; they helped people learn through schools broadcasts and documentaries; they brought music, sport, stories and entertainment into the home; programmes in all languages helped keep languages and cultures strong.
